title: Kinki rain risk is now specific: prepare before Thursday night
summary: Mas specific na ang risk kaysa kaninang update: Osaka Regional Headquarters says Kinki faces heavy rain from September 3-6, with central Kinki needing particular vigilance from late September 3 through the morning of September 4. Japan Weather Association says some locations could exceed 300 mm total rain.
why_it_matters: This is now more than a broad typhoon watch for Kinki. The official regional guidance identifies a near-term window for flooding, river rise and landslide risk, so low-cost preparation should be finished before Thursday night.

sources.publisher: Japan Meteorological Agency - Osaka Regional Headquarters
sources.title: 前線や台風第24号による天気の見通し
近畿 3日午後～5日は広く警報級大雨のおそれ 総雨量300ミリ以上の所も

claims.text: Osaka Regional Headquarters' September 2 briefing says Typhoon 24 is expected to remain slow-moving south of Japan near waters south of Kyushu through around September 7, feeding warm moist air into western Japan.
claims.basis: Official JMA regional briefing based on the September 2 11:00 forecast.

claims.text: The same JMA briefing warns of heavy rain from September 3 through around September 6 and says central Kinki should particularly guard against low-land flooding and river rise or flooding from late September 3 through the morning of September 4.
claims.basis: Official Osaka Regional Headquarters forecast briefing.

claims.text: Japan Weather Association says widespread warning-level heavy rain is possible in Kinki from the afternoon of September 3 through September 5, with total rainfall exceeding 100 mm widely and more than 300 mm in some locations.
claims.basis: Japan Weather Association forecast published September 2 at 12:44 JST.

claims.text: At 15:00 JST September 2, Typhoon 24 remained south of Japan, moving north slowly, with central pressure 996 hPa and maximum sustained winds 18 m/s.
claims.basis: Japan Weather Association reproduction of current typhoon data.

claims.text: For Kinki households, the useful preparation deadline has moved forward from a general September 3-6 watch to finishing basic preparation before late September 3, because the official forecast now identifies a specific higher-risk overnight window.
claims.basis: Practical timing inference from the newly specific official regional warning window.

content.key_message: If you are in Kinki, finish cheap flood/rain preparation before late September 3; the risk window is now specific enough to act on.

change_summary.previous: Earlier guidance supported broad PREPARE action for September 3-6, but exact mainland impacts and the highest-risk timing were still uncertain.
change_summary.now: JMA's Osaka Regional Headquarters now identifies heavy-rain risk through around September 6 and specifically flags central Kinki from late September 3 through the morning of September 4 for flooding and river hazards; JWA says some locations could exceed 300 mm total rainfall.
change_summary.why_change_matters: The update creates a concrete preparation deadline and a narrower period when unnecessary road travel and flood-prone parking deserve extra caution.

content.who_is_affected: People in Kinki, especially central Kinki and households near low-lying roads, rivers, slopes or known flood zones. Travelers using roads and rail in the region from September 3-5 should also monitor operator notices.
content.when: Rain risk increases September 3 and can persist through around September 6. Central Kinki's highlighted hazard window is late September 3 through the morning of September 4.
content.financial_impact: No defensible generic yen amount. The main avoidable losses are vehicle/property flood damage, disrupted travel and last-minute emergency purchases; actual exposure depends heavily on location.
content.risk_if_ignored: A car left in a known low-lying or flood-prone location, unnecessary driving during intense rain, or delayed evacuation from a locally warned area can turn a forecast inconvenience into a high-consequence loss or safety event.
content.deadline: For Kinki, finish basic preparation before late September 3 and recheck JMA warnings before sleep and before morning travel on September 4.
content.effort: Low: charge phones and power banks, secure outdoor items, check your municipal hazard map, avoid parking in known flood-prone low spots, and verify train/road conditions before travel.
content.potential_benefit: Better chance of avoiding dangerous travel, flooded parking and rushed purchases if local warnings escalate.
content.downside: Rainfall will vary sharply by location and 300 mm is not a region-wide forecast. Do not cancel everything solely from a regional headline; use JMA local warnings and Kikikuru for escalation decisions.
content.what_to_do_or_watch: Kinki residents: PREPARE before Thursday night. Use JMA warnings and Kikikuru for your municipality; if warning levels rise or transport suspensions are announced, reduce nonessential travel accordingly.
content.bottom_line: The broad Typhoon 24 watch has become a specific Kinki heavy-rain preparation call for Thursday night into Friday morning.
content.confidence_reason: High confidence in the regional risk window because it comes directly from JMA's Osaka Regional Headquarters; exact rainfall at any household remains location- and track-dependent.
content.what_would_change_mind: A substantial track/moisture shift plus downgraded JMA regional guidance would lower urgency. Local Level 3-5 evacuation information, linear rainband forecasts, rising Kikikuru risk or transport suspensions would raise the action from PREPARE to DO NOW in the affected municipality.

reading_levels.30 sec:
What happened: JMA now flags Kinki for heavy rain September 3-6, with central Kinki particularly at risk late September 3 through the morning of September 4. JWA says some places could exceed 300 mm total rain.
Why it matters: Flooding, river rise and transport disruption are now credible near-term risks.
What to do: Finish basic preparation before Thursday night and check local JMA warnings before travel.
Bottom line: PREPARE; escalate only when your local warnings justify it.
reading_levels.2_min: The Typhoon 24 story has materially changed for Kinki. Osaka Regional Headquarters says the slow-moving typhoon will keep feeding warm moist air into western Japan while a front moves south, creating heavy-rain risk from September 3 through around September 6. Central Kinki has a specifically highlighted period from late September 3 through the morning of September 4 for low-land flooding and river rise/flooding. Japan Weather Association adds that widespread totals above 100 mm are possible and some locations may exceed 300 mm. That 300 mm figure is not a forecast for every city. Practical action is simple: finish charging, outdoor-item securing, hazard-map checking and flood-prone parking decisions before Thursday night, then use local JMA warnings and Kikikuru rather than generic social-media storm maps.
